control.single_change: Override m1 R/Z quotient value, first derivative and second derivative with positive-node-only spline; physical m1 coefficient at the axis remains zero, but no axis value/jet is queried.
control.targets: Same four shells j=1,2,4,8; all s>=h=1/288. No extrapolation, tuning, new nodes or changes to supplied positive coefficients.
control.polynomial_identity: For q=a+b*s+c*s², linear q0=2q1-q2=a-2ch² makes full-grid not-a-knot q_spline_second(h)=0 exactly. Positive-node-only not-a-knot reproduces q and both derivatives exactly; f=sqrt(s)*q product derivatives are then exact at targets.
control.jet_scope: At each full-grid target, R/Z values and pure angular jets remain the supplied data; radial, radial-angular and radial-second jets may change. O(1) refers to quotient curvature error, not unscaled Cartesian second jets.
control.expected_signature: If first-shell force/J discrepancy falls materially while positive-node geometry values stay unchanged, the invented m1 quotient axis closure contributes. Lack of improvement refutes its dominance for this fixed control. Neither outcome repairs the BOOZ first-half input or qualifies the equilibrium.

algebra.native_axis: q0=2q(h)-q(2h)=a-2*c*h²; exact not-a-knot plus first interior relation forces fitted q_second(h)=0. True q_second=2*c.
algebra.infinite_grid_first_jet_errors: delta_q_prime(h)=c*h/sqrt(3); delta_f_second(h)=c*sqrt(h)*(-2+1/sqrt(3)). Finite far-boundary correction decays exponentially; quotient curvature error remains exactly -2*c.
algebra.BOOZ_first_half: 1.5*q(h)-0.5*q(2h)-q(h/2)=-3*c*h²/4; subsequent quotient midpoint averages have +c*h²/4 bias.
algebra.control_identity: Positive-node-only not-a-knot reproduces quadratic q and both derivatives exactly in exact arithmetic; no invented quotient axis sample. This manufactured identity does not imply actual source coefficients are quadratic.

independent_review.result: No concrete issue; m1 selection, product derivatives, baseline geometry ordering and saved-field comparison checked.

conclusion: Removing only the invented m1 quotient axis sample worsens the characteristic force on every tested shell. The exact zero-quotient-curvature closure is a real sensitivity, but this control refutes it as a sufficient recovery mechanism and does not justify a production or BOOZ repair.
limitations: One fixed source, native192x192 grid and four shells; no convergence or equilibrium qualification.
All positive source positions and pure angular first/second jets are bitwise unchanged; radial derivative reconstruction changes.
Raw BOOZ first-half transfer is unchanged, so this does not repair or separately measure its curvature bias.
All other geometry modes, lambda, flux/pressure profiles and frozen baseline artifacts remain unchanged.
No additional source/BOOZ runs, builds, filters, production changes or acceptance changes.
